name: Conjugated linoleic acid
short: Trials report constipation, diarrhoea and soft stools. One meta-analysis found small rises in fasting glucose and the liver enzyme AST; another found no change in liver enzymes.
text: In a meta-analysis of randomised trials lasting at least 6 months, the adverse events reported with conjugated linoleic acid (CLA) included constipation, diarrhoea and soft stools. A meta-analysis of 13 randomised trials in people at risk of cardiovascular disease found that CLA produced a small increase in fasting blood glucose (4.49 mg/dL) and in the liver enzyme AST, with no effect on HbA1c, insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) or ALT; the authors noted these effects were small and may not reach clinical importance, and a separate meta-analysis of 22 trials in adults found that ALT and AST did not change compared with control. An earlier systematic review of human trials reported that some studies observed adverse effects of CLA isomers on lipid profile (lower HDL cholesterol and higher Lp(a)) and on glucose metabolism, including insulin sensitivity, and called for long-term placebo-controlled trials of safety. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
